# Crew API schemas

The objects the [Crew API](README.md) endpoints send and receive, by name.

This page does not say what the gateway serves. Whether an endpoint is available now, and which of its fields are not served yet, is on the endpoint's own page.

|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | apr_ plus 128 random bits; unique across the instance. |
| `object` | `approval` | yes |  |

| `answerable_by_you` | boolean | no |  |
| `approval_url` | string (uri) | no | Address of the approval page (a proposal). The app hands it to the user, who signs in in a small window under the Kiro Crew host name and answers there. The app itself cannot answer. |

## ApprovalState

Only these four values are used. When a turn is cancelled, the approval it was waiting on becomes expired with reason turn_cancelled.

Type: `pending`, `allowed`, `denied`, `expired`.

## Bot

Roster and status, these fields only. It is the cut-down view apps get of the Owner tier's BotRosterRow (GET /v1/crew/owner/bots): only id, name, description, avatar, status and has_goal, and only the grant's Bot range. Private chat (including the last line), briefing, rules, conversations and private memory are never here, and no Public operation returns them.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Also the model value for /v1/responses. |
| `object` | `bot` | yes |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `description` | string | no |  |
| `avatar_url` | string or null | no |  |
| `status` | string: `idle`, `busy` | yes | busy means this Bot has a turn running right now (in whichever conversation). The values are the same as the App SDK's Bot. Open enum; a client treats an unknown value as idle. |
| `has_goal` | boolean | no | This Bot has a goal; when true, GET /v1/crew/bots/{bot_id}/goals has content to read. |
| `created_by_app` | boolean | no | true: this app created the Bot (bundle.kind bot or bots:create), so it is in the app_created range. |

## BotRoster

The full Bot roster as the owner sees it (GET /v1/crew/owner/bots, which wraps GET /api/members). One row per global Bot, with its private chat with the owner, its configuration and its live state. The Public GET /v1/crew/bots is the cut-down view apps get (Bot).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `members` | array of [BotRosterRow](schemas.md#botrosterrow) | yes | Field names follow what GET /api/members returns today; the wrapper does not change the shape. |

## BotRosterRow

One roster row. The fields are the ones GET /api/members returns today; the Owner tier is experimental, so fields can be added later. Free text other than name and slug goes through the gateway's redaction and can be replaced as a whole.

| `slot_key` | string | yes | The session key of the private chat with the owner; an empty string while that chat has not been opened. |

| `grant_wakes_this_hour` | integer | yes |  |
| `grant_wake_limit_per_hour` | integer | yes | 120 by default (a proposal); the user can lower it. |
| `credits_used_today` | number or null | no |  |
| `daily_credits` | number or null | no |  |

## ConnectorManifest

What the user agreed to for this app: its capability bundle, scopes and webhook address.

| `entitlements` | array of [Entitlement](schemas.md#entitlement) | no | The entitlements the app wants; they are written to the registration record and signed into the token's ent only after Kiro reviews them. |
| `scopes` | array of string | yes |  |
| `optional_scopes` | array of `memory:read`, `knowledge:read`, `schedules:manage`, `workflows:run` | no |  |
| `requested_quota` | object | no | Defaults apply when omitted. The default tier allows at most 50 credits a day; with quota.elevated, at most 500; the user sets the final number on the consent page. |

| `callbacks` | object | yes |  |

## CreateResponseRequest

Rule: support what can be done; refuse with 400 what would change what runs or what is stored (tools outside the manifest, `store: false`, unsupported tool types, `prompt`); accept and ignore fields that only tune generation or do bookkeeping, and list them in the response's `crew.ignored_parameters`. Phase 2 fields (images, files, json_schema, reasoning summaries) open per agent as `GET /v1/crew/capabilities` reports; when the agent does not support one, 422 `capability_unavailable`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model` | string | yes | For a delegated credential: the template id of the app's capability bundle, \<client_id>/\<bundle.agent.id>, or a bot id in the grant's bots. The owner may also pass a template name. Anything else gets 404 model_not_found. |
| `input` | string or array of [InputItem](schemas.md#inputitem) | yes |  |
| `instructions` | string | no | Appended after the agent's own prompt; cannot replace it. |
| `conversation` | string | no | Omit to create a new conversation. |
| `previous_response_id` | string | no | Either this or conversation; if both are given they must point to the same conversation, else 400. |
| `stream` | boolean (default `false`) | no |  |
| `background` | boolean (default `false`) | no | Returns queued at once. A background run started by a delegated credential holds a 5-minute lease; if the grant can no longer be verified when the lease runs out, the run ends incomplete with reason grant_unverified. |
| `metadata` | [Metadata](schemas.md#metadata) | no | At most 16 pairs; keys up to 64 characters, values up to 512 (same as OpenAI). |
| `tools` | array of [Tool](schemas.md#tool) | no | Without it, every tool in the consented manifest is used. `web_search`, `file_search`, `code_interpreter`, `computer_use` and `image_generation` get 400 `unsupported_tool_type`. |
| `tool_choice` | `auto`, `none` | no |  |
| `store` | `true` | no | Only true is accepted; false gets 400. |
| `text` | object | no | Output format: `text` (phase 1) or `json_schema` (phase 2, only when the agent's `structured_output` is true). |
| `reasoning` | object | no | Reasoning summary (phase 2), off by default: without this field no reasoning item is returned. Summaries only, never the raw reasoning. A level that is not in the agent's `reasoning_summary` is 422 capability_unavailable. |
| `temperature` | number | no | Accepted and ignored; listed in crew.ignored_parameters. |
| `top_p` | number | no | Accepted and ignored. |
| `max_output_tokens` | integer | no | Accepted and ignored. |

## Entitlement

What Kiro allows an app to ask for. It is a second gate beside scope: an entitlement decides whether the app may ask, a scope whether the user granted it. The crew checks ent from phase 1 on; phase 1 has only local-development entitlements, which an owner sets for apps they registered themselves; review by Kiro starts in phase 2. Open enum.

Type: `memory.read`, `memory.global`, `knowledge.read`, `workflows.run`, `schedules.manage`, `notifications.send`, `quota.elevated`, `bots.create`.

## Error

Unified error body. Shape follows OpenAI. Clients treat an unknown code by its HTTP status.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | object | yes |  |

## ErrorCode

Open enum: a client treats an unknown code by its HTTP status. The examples are the known values, not all of them; the table is in the RFC. stale_session_reauth (401): this first-party session signed in before an owner was configured, the owner check does not accept it, and the user has to sign in again. grant_paused is 403 (the user has to resume it; it is not rate limiting). prune_in_progress (503): the Bot roster is being tidied; retry later.

Type: string.

## ErrorType

Open enum: clients must accept unknown values. The examples are the known values, not all of them.

Type: string.

## Event

In-instance event. Types and fields are only ever added; clients skip unknown types but still advance their cursor.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seq` | integer | yes | Strictly increasing within this stream. A conversation stream has one numbering per conversation; the instance stream is numbered separately for each grant, so an app cannot read activity elsewhere from the numbers. Gaps can still occur within one stream, and a client must not treat a gap as a loss. |
| `event_id` | string | yes | Globally unique; deduplicate across streams, push and replay by it. |
| `type` | string: `conversation.created`, `conversation.updated`, `turn.started`, `message.created`, `tool.called`, `tool.completed`, `plan.updated`, `approval.requested`, `approval.decided`, `turn.completed`, `grant.revoked`, `notice`, `bot.reply`, `bot.turn.completed` | yes | Open enum. |
| `conversation` | string or null | no |  |
| `response` | string or null | no |  |
| `created_at` | [Timestamp](schemas.md#timestamp) | yes | Unix seconds. |
| `data` | object | yes |  |

## GrantRequest

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `object` | `grant_request` | yes |  |
| `namespace` | `default` | yes | The group this record belongs to. Stored on every record; today it has one fixed value. |
| `status` | [GrantRequestStatus](schemas.md#grantrequeststatus) | yes |  |
| `client_id` | string | yes | As the app reported it |
| `client_name` | string | no | As the app reported it; the first 80 characters of client_id when the app sent none |
| `verified` | `false` | no | Always false: a program on this machine reported the name and client_id, and nothing verified them |
| `redirect_uri` | string (uri) | no | The loopback address the authorization code goes to |
| `user_code` | string | no | Short code the app shows, so the owner can tell which request is which |
| `requested_scopes` | array of string | yes |  |
| `requested_bots` | array of string | no | The Bot names the app sends as the repeated bots query parameter of GET /oauth/authorize, one Bot per occurrence, without splitting; empty when omitted. The app is expected to send the exact model id from GET /v1/models. Names follow kiro_crew.members.is_dispatchable_member_name with the MEMBER_NAME_MAX_CHARS length limit; duplicates are refused. Asking checks format, never existence. Malformed bots gives 400 invalid_request even with an invalid scope. Asking again requires the same bots values in the same order. MAX_REQUESTED_BOTS is the chosen bound for one request and one decision, set equal to crew_teams.TEAM_MEMBERS_MAX (500), the largest Bot list the product keeps elsewhere. The request must fit aiohttp's 8190-byte request line. The decision body must fit 4 KiB (_BODY_MAX); a bots list that does not fit gives 400 invalid_request, and the owner gives a shorter list. |
| `created_at` | [Timestamp](schemas.md#timestamp) | yes | Unix seconds. |
| `expires_at` | [Timestamp](schemas.md#timestamp) | yes | Unix seconds. |
| `decided_at` | integer or null | no | When the owner answered (amendment, proposed) |
| `decided_by` | object or null | no | Who answered: the kind of caller, never a token (amendment, proposed) |
| `granted_scopes` | array of string | no | Only when approved; what the owner gave, which may be fewer than requested (amendment, proposed) |
| `granted_bots` | array of string | no | Only when approved; the Bot names the owner gave, which may be none. They become the grant's bots with mode selected. Names follow kiro_crew.members.is_dispatchable_member_name and MEMBER_NAME_MAX_CHARS, with no duplicates. MAX_REQUESTED_BOTS is the chosen bound for one request and one decision, set equal to crew_teams.TEAM_MEMBERS_MAX (500), the largest Bot list the product keeps elsewhere. The decision body must fit 4 KiB (_BODY_MAX); a bots list that does not fit gives 400 invalid_request, and the owner gives a shorter list. The decision checks expiry, pending status and the requested subset before reading the roster. The grants list returns the owner's recorded selection; no route enforces it yet. |
| `grant_id` | string or null | no | The grant this request led to, set once the app redeemed its code (amendment, proposed) |

## GrantRequestDecision

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `decision` | `approve`, `deny` | yes |  |
| `scopes` | array of string | no | Only with approve: the scopes to give. Must be a subset of requested_scopes. Left out: all requested scopes. |
| `bots` | array of string | no | Only with approve: a JSON array of exact Bot names from GET /v1/models, a subset of requested_bots. Names follow kiro_crew.members.is_dispatchable_member_name and MEMBER_NAME_MAX_CHARS, with no duplicates. MAX_REQUESTED_BOTS is the chosen bound for one request and one decision, set equal to crew_teams.TEAM_MEMBERS_MAX (500), the largest Bot list the product keeps elsewhere. The decision body must fit 4 KiB (_BODY_MAX); a bots list that does not fit gives 400 invalid_request, and the owner gives a shorter list. After the body's size, decision and scopes form (each 400 invalid_request), the handler checks the request before any Bot check (404 not_found if unknown or expired, 409 grant_request_already_resolved if answered), then the requested subset, then the roster. Each Bot must exist in that read. When an approval gives at least one Bot, unreadable configuration or a degraded Bot roster gives 503 instance_unavailable without recording a decision. An approval that gives none, and a deny, do not read the roster. Asking via GET /oauth/authorize uses repeated bots query parameters, one Bot per occurrence, and checks format only, never existence; asking again requires the same values in the same order. Left out: no Bot, because a Bot is never given by default. Explicit null gives 400 invalid_request (bots must be a list of strings). On a deny, the server ignores bots whatever its value, even though the schema declares an array. |

## ResponseStreamEvent

SSE events of `POST /v1/responses` (stream=true) and `GET /v1/responses/{id}?stream=true`. Each SSE `event:` line carries the type and each `data:` line is this object as JSON. `sequence_number` increases only within this turn's stream and is used by `starting_after`; it is unrelated to the event stream's `seq`. `response.reasoning_summary_*` is sent only when the request carries reasoning.summary (phase 2). Not sent: `response.reasoning_text.*`, `response.refusal.*`, `response.output_text.annotation.added`, `response.web_search_call.*`, `response.file_search_call.*`, `response.code_interpreter_call.*`, `response.image_generation_call.*`. Clients skip `crew.*` events they do not know.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `response.created`, `response.queued`, `response.in_progress`, `response.completed`, `response.failed`, `response.incomplete`, `response.output_item.added`, `response.output_item.done`, `response.content_part.added`, `response.content_part.done`, `response.output_text.delta`, `response.output_text.done`, `response.function_call_arguments.delta`, `response.function_call_arguments.done`, `response.mcp_call.in_progress`, `response.mcp_call.completed`, `response.mcp_call.failed`, `response.reasoning_summary_part.added`, `response.reasoning_summary_part.done`, `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta`, `response.reasoning_summary_text.done`, `error`, `crew.notice` | yes |  |
| `sequence_number` | integer (at least 0) | yes |  |
| `response` | [Response](schemas.md#response) | no | For response.* lifecycle events. |
| `output_index` | integer | no |  |
| `content_index` | integer | no |  |
| `item_id` | string | no |  |

| `part` | [OutputText](schemas.md#outputtext) | no |  |
| `delta` | string | no |  |
| `text` | string | no |  |

## UpdateGrantRequest

Tighten only: quota and wake limits can only go down, bots can only be removed, and status can only be set to paused. Raising a limit or adding a Bot is 403 insufficient_scope (the app has to start a new consent); resuming is POST /v1/crew/owner/grants/{grant_id}/resume.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `paused` | no | The owner pauses this app in one step: the grant records pause.by user. After that a wake is 403 grant_paused, a tool call returns the tool error grant_paused, and queued wakes are dropped. |
| `wake_limits` | [WakeLimits](schemas.md#wakelimits) | no |  |
| `quota` | object | no |  |
| `monitor` | object | no |  |
| `notify_per_hour` | integer (at least 0) | no |  |
| `bots` | object | no | Bots can be removed only with mode selected; changing the mode needs a new consent. |
